diagnostic_evidence.quote: Any minimizer $\hat{ \bm{c} }$ of \eqref{eq:wSR-LASSO} with the intrinsic weights

issues.failure_explanation: The weighted l1-'norm' is defined as the linear functional sum_i w_i z_i with no absolute values. It is not a norm (it takes negative values and fails absolute homogeneity), and the decoders built from it are not sparsity-promoting: along z = -t w the weighted SR-LASSO objective behaves as t(||Psi w||_2 - lambda||w||_2^2), which tends to -infinity whenever lambda||w||_2^2 > ||Psi w||_2. That regime includes the setting of Corollary cor:CS, where lambda = 1/(8 sqrt(tilde m)) and the intrinsic weights w_nu = ||psi_nu||_infinity >= 1 give ||w||_2 >= sqrt(N) with N >> tilde m. Hence minimizers of eq:wSR-LASSO need not exist as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert absolute values, i.e. define ||z||_{1,w} := sum_i w_i |z_i| (the standard weighted l1-norm used in the cited literature); with this forced correction the decoders, Corollary cor:CS and Remark rem:wQCBP_extension stand as stated.
issues.overall_effect: The weighted SR-LASSO and weighted QCBP estimators (eq:wSR-LASSO, eq:wqcbp) are ill-defined as written: the SR-LASSO objective can be unbounded below, so 'any minimizer' in the guarantee of Corollary cor:CS (and its QCBP extension in Remark rem:wQCBP_extension) may quantify over an empty set.
issues.title: Weighted l1-norm defined without absolute values, making the weighted decoders ill-posed
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction (restore the absolute values in the norm) repairs the decoder construction; no rate, guarantee type, or scope is lost and no new argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exist a compact set $\mathcal{K}\subset \mathbb{C}^d$, with $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathcal{K}$
$\mathcal{K} = \mathcal{E}_{\bm{\rho}'}$, where $\bm{\rho}' > \bm{\rho}$ (strict inequality applies to every component)

We define a holomorphic extension $\tilde{\bm{f}}$ in a natural way using the complex-valued extension $\tilde{\bm{C}}$ to $\bm{C}$, whose existence is guaranteed by Assumption~\ref{ass:diffusion_matrix}.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem assumes Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix 'for some compact K such that K subset U', but that Assumption requires U subset K. Together the two inclusions force K = U = [-1,1]^d, a subset of R^d whose interior in C^d is empty, so the stated conclusions (a holomorphic extension to the interior of K, and the uniform bound over arbitrary compact H contained in that interior) are vacuous. The proof itself needs the opposite inclusion: it defines tilde f by restricting tilde C from [0,T] x K to [0,T] x U, and all downstream corollaries apply the theorem with E_rho subset interior(K), which is incompatible with K subset U.

failure_location.quote: satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:diffusion_matrix} for some compact $\mathcal{K}\subseteq\C^d$ such that $\mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{U}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'K \subset \mathcal{U}' with '\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{K}' (equivalently delete the clause, since Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix already imposes U subset K); the given proof and all three corollaries then apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the paper's central holomorphy theorem has a hypothesis inconsistent with the assumption it invokes and delivers no usable content; Corollaries cor:maincor, cor:LS and cor:CS, which all invoke the theorem in the regime U subset E_rho subset interior(K), lose their stated foundation.
issues.title: Main theorem assumes the reversed inclusion K subset U, contradicting Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix and vacuating the conclusion
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced inclusion reversal already dictated by the invoked assumption and by the proof; every substantive claim, rate, and dependent result survives with no new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated least-squares bound has no factor depending on the magnitude of f_v. Since problem eq:ted is linear in u_0, scaling u_0 by lambda scales f_v, the noiseless data, and hence the least-squares error by |lambda| (on the same good sampling event, with the same witness set S), while the right-hand side C(rho,p)(m/log(m/epsilon))^{1/2-1/p} is unchanged. For any instance with nonzero approximation error (the paper's own experiments report nonzero RMSE), the inequality therefore fails for large |lambda|. All invoked ingredients carry the missing factor: eq:bounderror is proportional to ||f||_{L^infty(E_rho)}, Theorem thm:mainthm bounds this by B(u_0,T,M), and the parallel compressed-sensing Corollary cor:CS includes B(u_0,T,rho,M) explicitly. The same omission occurs in the supporting Theorem th:main_ls.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply the approximation term by ||tilde f_v||_{L^infty(E_rho)}, bounded by B(u_0,T,M) from Theorem thm:mainthm with H = E_rho -- exactly as done in Corollary cor:CS -- and correspondingly insert the factor ||f||_{L^infty(E_rho)} in Theorem th:main_ls; the algebraic rate (m/log(m/epsilon))^{1/2-1/p} is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The least-squares guarantee of Corollary cor:LS (and the appendix Theorem th:main_ls on which it rests) is false as stated over its quantified class of problems: it cannot hold uniformly as ||u_0|| grows, so the advertised quasi-optimal LS rate is only valid after the missing problem-dependent factor is reinstated.
issues.title: Least-squares error bound missing the sup-norm factor B(u0,T,M), making it false under scaling of the initial data
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line insertion of a factor already established in the paper (Theorem thm:mainthm) and used verbatim in the sibling Corollary cor:CS; no new lemma, no rate loss, and no change of scope is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\varrho$ be either the uniform or Chebyschev measure on $\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d$
$\{\psi_{\bm{\nu}} \}_{\bm{\nu}\in\mathbb{N}_0^d}$ a family of orthonormal polynomials over $L^2_{\varrho}(\mathcal{U})$

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficients of the L^2_rho-orthonormal expansion are c_nu = integral f psi_nu d rho, but the proof computes plain Lebesgue integrals and relies on integral_{-1}^1 psi_{nu_k}(x_k) dx_k = 0. For the Chebyshev basis -- which is orthonormal with respect to the Chebyshev measure, not Lebesgue measure -- this is false: e.g. integral_{-1}^1 sqrt(2) T_{2j}(x) dx = -2 sqrt(2)/(4j^2-1), which is nonzero, and integral f psi_nu dx is not even the expansion coefficient. Thus the vanishing-coefficient computation that reduces the support S to N_0^d x {0}^N is invalid as written for the Chebyshev case that the theorem explicitly covers (only the uniform/Legendre case, where d rho is proportional to dx, is correctly argued).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write the coefficients with respect to the sampling measure, c_nu = integral f psi_nu d rho, and replace the last step by orthonormality: integral_{-1}^1 psi_{nu_k} d rho = <psi_{nu_k}, psi_0>_{L^2_rho} = 0 for nu_k nonzero, which holds for both the uniform and Chebyshev measures; the factorization argument is otherwise unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem th:main_ls is unproved as written for the Chebyshev measure, and consequently the proof of Corollary cor:LS (which allows either basis and routes through Theorem th:main_ls) has a gap in the Chebyshev case.
issues.title: Appendix proof of Theorem th:main_ls uses Lebesgue integrals; the key vanishing step is false for the Chebyshev basis
issues.why_classification: A forced, local repair of one displayed computation (integrate against d rho instead of dx and invoke orthonormality) restores the proof; the theorem's conclusion and its downstream use in Corollary cor:LS are unchanged.
